business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–United States Trade Promotion Agreement (2012, investment chapter)
Colombia–European Union Trade Agreement (2013, investment protection provisions)
Colombia–United Kingdom Trade and Investment Agreement (2021)
Colombia–Canada Free Trade Agreement (2011, investment chapter)
Colombia–Spain Bilateral Investment Treaty (2008) and Double Taxation Agreement (2008)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF creation and AML/CFT framework); Law 1121 of 2006 (FATF alignment); Law 1762 of 2015 (AML and anti-bribery reforms, beneficial ownership duties); DIAN Resolution 000164 of 2020 (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - RUBF); Superintendencia de Sociedades Circular Basica Juridica as amended (UBO reporting duties of commercial companies); Decree 1074 of 2015 (Single Business Registry RUES and Chamber of Commerce procedure); Law 455 of 1998 (accession to Hague Apostille Convention).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and current Articles (estatutos) of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry of the shareholder's country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State, or equivalent)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under Law 455 of 1998; consular legalization only for non-apostille signatory states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney appointing the Colombian incorporator and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille followed by certified Spanish translation in Colombia

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each shareholder and final beneficial owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National issuing authority of the holder's country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy; if executed abroad, apostille or notarial certification with certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or of existence and legal representation of any legal-entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Chamber of Commerce or equivalent registry of the shareholder's domicile
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate resolution of the foreign shareholder authorizing the S.A.S. incorporation and capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board/shareholder meeting of the foreign entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille and certified Spanish translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signing screening of every incorporator, shareholder, director, legal representative, and UBO against: (i) OFAC SDN List and the 50% ownership rule; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated lists under Resolutions 1267, 1988, and 1373; (iii) EU consolidated financial sanctions lists; (iv) Colombian domestic lists maintained by UIAF and Fiscalia General; (v) the Procuraduria disciplinary sanctions database; and (vi) INTERPOL Red Notices. The supervising counsel, the notary, and the Chamber of Commerce each perform an independent screen; any positive hit triggers automatic refusal, suspension of the incorporation, and filing of a suspicious transaction report. A signed negative PEP/OFAC certification is archived in the incorporation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Unico Empresarial y Social (RUES) operated through the local Camara de Comercio virtual portal (e.g., Camara de Comercio de Bogota - CCB Virtual; Camara de Comercio de Medellin for Antioquia; and all regional chambers)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in Spanish. Foreign-language words are admissible only when registered as a trademark or transliterated into Latin script without confusing diacritics, and the name may not consist solely of a foreign term lacking Spanish readability. The exact registered Spanish transliteration must be identical in the articles, the RUES filing, and the certificate of existence and legal representation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 business days of the negative homonimia/similarity notification, the incorporator files a written reconsideration (recurso de reposicion) with the same Chamber of Commerce. If denied, a supplementary appeal (recurso de apelacion) may be filed with the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within 5 business days under Decree 1074 of 2015. Alternatively, the incorporator may immediately lodge a revised name as a provisional reservation; lodging the revised name before the appeal deadline expires preserves filing priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permitted. The Chamber of Commerce accepts a virtual office address for correspondence and notifications, but the S.A.S. must declare and maintain a physical principal place of business in Colombia for tax domicile (DIAN), legal service of process, and accounting records. For a remote cybersecurity SaaS with no local employees, a licensed virtual office with physical mail-handling and a commercial sublease service agreement is acceptable; a mere postal mailbox without legal support infrastructure is not accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. Estimated 5% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 12 months for a Low_Risk_Standard tier entity. The risk rises to approximately 20% if the company declares no physical Colombian location, uses only a mailbox address, or if the UBO resides in or is a national of a high-risk jurisdiction.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name search, homonimia check, and name reservation certificate — per selected name
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Camara de Comercio (e.g., Camara de Comercio de Bogota)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory chamber tariff published in UVT units; prevailing market rate USD 10-30

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Single-window filing of S.A.S. incorporation and merchant registration (Matricula Mercantil) including RUES administrative fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff scaled by declared assets and income; small-entity estimate for a de minimis capital S.A.S.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notary fees for legalization of private-document articles and signatures on the corporate books registration
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notaria (Notary Public) — optional for private-document S.A.S.; mandatory only if real property is contributed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff table of the Superintendencia de Notariado y Registro

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional public deed (escritura publica) if shareholders elect deed form instead of private statute
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff per capital range; prevailing market USD 50-150

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille bundle for 3-5 foreign corporate documents (certificate of incorporation, powers of attorney, board resolutions, good standing certificates)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent apostille authority in the country of origin (e.g., U.S. Department of State or Secretary of State)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing government fee per apostille (USD 15-40 each) plus courier and handling

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official certified Spanish translation of apostilled foreign documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Traductor Oficial registered with the Colombian Ministry of Foreign Affairs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 15-40 per translated page

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal counsel — drafting S.A.S. bylaws (estatutos), UBO piercing diligence, PEP/OFAC screening, and AML compliance pack
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing flat market fee for a standard S.A.S. incorporation with foreign shareholders

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUT (NIT/Tax ID) pre-registration and DIAN electronic signature e-files
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RUBF UBO filing and shareholders book (libro de socios) preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External accountant assigned on formation; government RUBF filing fee is zero
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark professional fee for preparation; statutory RUBF registration has no government cost

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of existence and legal representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representacion Legal) for bank and registry use

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), Articles 1-49; Colombian Commercial Code (Código de Comercio), Articles 353-371; Decree 410/1971 and Decree 1074/2015.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce) via the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES); DIAN for tax registration and NIT issuance.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución de Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada (private incorporation document), optionally raised to a public deed before a Notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-in capital is required under Law 1258/2008. The full subscribed capital must be paid within two years after incorporation; no escrow account is mandated for cash contributions, and contributions in kind may be made without prior appraisal unless otherwise required by law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the incorporation deed submitted to Cámara de Comercio is approved and the whole issued share capital is subscribed by the founding shareholders as stated in the bylaws. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is fixed at the address set forth in the certificates of incorporation and domicile. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the following officers are appointed: the legal representative (representante legal) shall have the powers specified in the bylaws, and the alternate legal representative and principal corporate officer are appointed to act as necessary. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the officers are authorized to obtain the tax identification number, open bank accounts, register as an employer, and take any ancillary steps to commence operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability Search and Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social / Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the commercial registry to verify the requested corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing one. Submit the name reservation request through RUES or in person at the Chamber, and obtain a reservation certificate valid for approximately 30 days.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if acting through an appointed agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or reserved, file a new request for an alternate name or challenge the similarity decision before the Chamber of Commerce within the statutory response period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of the Constitutional Documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (if public deed is used) or Cámara de Comercio (for private incorporation document).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the private incorporation document or public deed containing the complete bylaws of the S.A.S., including corporate purpose, share capital, representation structure, and term. Have the founding shareholders sign the document; if a public deed is used, obtain notarial certification. Present the document for pre-registration review at the Chamber if required.
required_dossiers: List of shareholders with capital subscription details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any drafting or notarial defects by executing a supplemental document or aclaratory act and resubmitting within the Chamber's term for correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry Filing and Certificate of Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (Chamber of Commerce) through RUES.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the constitutional document and supporting forms to the Chamber of Commerce for registration in the merchant registry. Pay the registration fee and obtain the Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal), which serves as proof of incorporation.
required_dossiers: Board resolution if appointing initial officers
Legal representative's identity card and address information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a requerimiento for defects, rectify the specified omissions and resubmit the corrected instrument within the legal curing period; appeal the refusal if the Chamber exceeds authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (through DIAN's virtual processing office).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register with DIAN to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and the RUT (Registro Único Tributario). Indicate the company's principal economic activity under ISIC 6201/NAICS 541512 and complete the tax registry forms, including the estimated income tax regime and invoicing requirements.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation from the Chamber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to any DIAN information requirement within one month by submitting the missing data; request correction or reconsideration if the RUT classification is inaccurate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account and Employer Registration Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Superintendencia Financiera supervised financial institutions; Caja de Compensación / PILA for payroll and social security enrollments.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a Colombian corporate bank account with the NIT and constitutional documents. If employees will be engaged, register the company with the social security system (EPS, ARL, Pension) and the payroll mechanism (PILA). Execute any required Board resolution authorizing the account officers and signatories.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation
Board resolution opening bank accounts and designating officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Resolve bank KYC or compliance inquiries by providing updated certifications, amended bylaws, or additional corporate transparency forms; for social security issues, correct errors through the PILA transaction process.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for a SaaS service provider. General corporate oversight is exercised by the Superintendencia de Sociedades and the Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating or manufacturing license is required for cybersecurity SaaS activities. The valid operation is based on the Chamber of Commerce registration, the RUT/NIT, and compliance with data protection rules under Law 1581/2012.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible (functionally exercised through local territorial environmental authorities; ANLA for large-scale projects only).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not required for pure software-as-a-service operations without physical installations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No specific industrial discharge, VOC, or wastewater limits apply to office-based SaaS activities. Domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewage disposal regulations, and electronic waste, including servers and equipment, must be handled through authorized e-waste collectors in accordance with Resolution 1511/2010.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office premises must obtain a fire safety inspection certificate from the local fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos) if a physical office is occupied. Structural compliance with the national earthquake-resistant building code (NSR-10) applies to leased or owned office space. If employees are engaged, the company must register with an ARL and implement the minimum occupational health and safety program under Resolution 0312/2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) — the national tax and customs authority of Colombia; online portal: www.dian.gov.co, with transactional services via the MUISCA platform and the SIRE electronic invoicing system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Colombian S.A.S., incorporation is effected by executing a constitutive private document under Law 1258 of 2008, filed with the Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (single business window). Once the company is registered, the S.A.S. must enroll in the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) maintained by DIAN. The process is performed using the online pre-registration module on the DIAN portal, followed by in-person biometric validation of the legal representative at an authorized DIAN service office or through an accredited intermediary. Upon completion, DIAN assigns the Número de Identificación Tributaria (NIT), a permanent ten-digit tax identification code, and simultaneously activates the S.A.S. as a common-regime IVA taxpayer, income-tax filer, customs declarant, and withholding agent. A Colombian resident legal representative with full tax filing powers is mandatory; non-resident shareholders are permitted and hold no ban on ownership, but the entity must maintain a valid resident fiscal representative to keep the NIT active and to receive DIAN notifications.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia does not provide a US-style check-the-box elective regime; entity classification follows commercial form, and an S.A.S. is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to entity-level corporate income tax. The principal statutory elections available are: (1) option to be taxed under the Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLES) established by Articles 903-916 of the Estatuto Tributario, available to an S.A.S. with gross income not exceeding COP 3,500,000,000, replacing ordinary CIT with a unified turnover-type tax; (2) designation as a Zona Franca (Free Trade Zone) taxpayer, where eligible, resulting in a reduced 20% CIT rate and special VAT treatment for the development of export-oriented software services; (3) formal election of the 0% VAT export treatment for services under Article 481 E.T., by registering the service-export activity in the RUT, filing the corresponding export declarations, and maintaining qualifying evidence; (4) application of the CFC and hybrid-mismatch transparency rules under Law 1819/2016, including the option to demonstrate effective substance for foreign-controlled entities; and (5) conclusion of advance pricing agreements (APAs) with DIAN for cross-border related-party service transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA — Impuesto al Valor Agregado (Impuesto sobre las Ventas), regulated under Articles 420 to 481 of the Estatuto Tributario and the IVA sections of Decree 1625 of 2016.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: An S.A.S. must register as an IVA responsible taxpayer (declarante) when, in the immediately preceding taxable year, its gross common taxable income exceeded COP 100,000,000 (approximately USD 23,000) or its year-end gross assets exceeded COP 350,000,000 (approximately USD 82,000). Because a cybersecurity SaaS business habitually supplies taxable digital services in Colombia, the S.A.S. will in practice be obliged to register as a common-regime IVA responsible regardless of those monetary thresholds. Registration is also a precondition for claiming the 0% export rate and the refund of input VAT credits on export activities.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic invoicing (Factura Electrónica de Venta — FEV) is fully mandatory for all VAT-responsible taxpayers, with the obligation phased to completion for all registered businesses by fiscal year 2024. The S.A.S. must contract with a DIAN-authorized technology provider (proveedor tecnológico) that transmits invoices in real time over SOAP/REST APIs to DIAN's validation service (Servicio de Validación Previa). Each FEV must bear the DIAN-assigned CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica) digital stamp, a QR code, and the standardized XML/XAdES structure set out in the Anexo Técnico, currently version 1.6, with migration underway to the SIRE document-electrónico platform (versions 2.0/2.1). DIAN performs real-time pre-clearance validation before an invoice reaches definitive status; rejected files must be corrected within the same business day. In addition, the S.A.S. must transmit the electronic invoicing data set to the 'Activo en Comercio' report, file monthly/quarterly form 300 (IVA return), submit form 2241 fiscal reconciliation, and, for services exports, coordinate with the VUCE (Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior) for the export declaration.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The cybersecurity SaaS offering (ISIC 6201 — cloud vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and related compliance SaaS) qualifies for the 0% IVA rate as an export of services under Article 481(4) of the Estatuto Tributario and Decree 1625/2016, Article 1.2.1.1.24, where the following cumulative conditions are met: (1) the customer is not domiciled in Colombia and is not a Colombian permanent establishment or resident related party; (2) the service is used or commercially exploited exclusively outside Colombian territory — for cloud SaaS, the software platform must operate from servers and data nodes located outside Colombia, and no Colombian user may benefit from the vulnerability scans or penetration-testing deliverables; (3) any associated professional/implementation services are rendered from Colombian offices to the foreign customer without interposition of a Colombian intermediary; (4) the consideration is received in freely convertible foreign currency (USD/EUR via Stripe or wire transfer) and is brought into the Colombian foreign-exchange market within the statutory repatriation period; and (5) the S.A.S. maintains a complete evidentiary file demonstrating offshore utilization, including IP-geolocation logs, server-location records, customer delivery receipts, and the contractual terms identifying the foreign recipient. The S.A.S. must formalize its service-export status in the RUT, file the corresponding service-export declarations, and may be required to obtain the exporter-of-services qualification certificate ('certificado de exportador de servicios') from the relevant authorities.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: DIAN Declaración de Exportación de Servicios (service export declaration) filed through VUCE (Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior), or DIAN form 4840 where applicable

Factura Comercial / Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV) evidencing the export transaction, including the SaaS subscription or penetration-testing services agreement, ISIC 6201 description, the foreign customer's legal identity and foreign VAT/GST registration number, and USD/EUR consideration
Signed SaaS master subscription agreement, order form, or marketplace procurement record containing exclusive offshore-delivery terms and the customer's foreign-domicile certification

Bill of Lading (B/L) or Air Waybill (AWB) when physical hardware, token media, or on-premise scanning appliances are shipped; otherwise, the digital delivery log capturing the encrypted download, customer consumption, and hosted-data-center location outside Colombia

Declaración de Cambio / Form ECO (inward foreign-exchange declaration), also known as the Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas, issued by the Colombian intermediary bank evidencing the USD/EUR inward remittance received through the Colombian foreign-exchange market
Cámara de Comercio / ColombiaProductiva certificate of exporter-of-services qualification (when issued) and the updated RUT evidencing the service-export activity code

Technical service-delivery evidence pack: penetration-test report transmittal receipt, vulnerability-assessment delivery emails, cloud provider region metadata, SIEM or API access logs, and user geolocation analytics demonstrating exclusive offshore usage
Supporting bank statements and payment reconciliations linking each invoice to the foreign-exchange repatriation certificates
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN subjects zero-rated service exports to intense documentary scrutiny, cross-matching the 0% claims against electronic invoices, VUCE declarations, RUT records, and bank foreign-exchange forms. Failure to substantiate any element of the export treatment results in: (a) retrospective reversal of the 0% rating, recharacterization of the income as locally taxable services, and assessment of the full 19% IVA on the export consideration, together with mora interest at the certified Banco de la República rate and the inaccuracy penalty under Article 648 E.T. of 130% of the assessed differential, increased to a higher punitive bracket — commonly 200% — where DIAN finds sham transactions, concealed facts, or deliberately fraudulent documentation; (b) clawback of all input VAT credits previously claimed as saldo a favor, disallowance of refunds, and exclusion from the automatic-refund regime for up to three taxable years; (c) criminal exposure under Law 1762 of 2015 for customs and tax fraud, including imprisonment and monetary fines for statutory tax evasion; (d) customs penalties under Decree 1165 of 2019 for inaccurate export declarations, potentially escalating to fines of up to 300% of the export value and suspension of the exporter's customs authorization; and (e) foreign-exchange sanctions imposed by the Central Bank for failure to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days, including fines equal to up to 200% of the un-repatriated amount, compulsory reintegration, and, in serious repeat cases, exclusion of the company from the Colombian foreign-exchange market.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), exercising foreign-exchange control through its Junta Directiva (Board of Directors) and the Comisión de Cambios; the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia supervises all authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries (local commercial banks and exchange houses); the DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) enforces the tax and customs formalities connected with cross-border payments and remittances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the mercantile registry (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the company's registered office (Cámara de Comercio, e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; the Chamber opens the renewal window on 1 January.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers Chamber fines under the Colombian Commercial Code; persistent non-renewal may lead to cancellation of the mercantile registration and, ultimately, administrative strike-off of the registered company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filing due in the March–May period following the fiscal year end; the exact cut-off date is assigned by DIAN on the basis of the taxpayer's NIT last digit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty accrues at 5% of the tax payable for each month or fraction of a month, up to 100% of the tax; default interest is charged, and continued non-filing allows DIAN to issue an official assessment and commence coercive collection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual financial statements and shareholders' meeting minutes (Depósito de Estados Financieros y Acta de Asamblea)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Chamber of Commerce of the corporate domicile and, if the audit or supervision threshold is met, the Superintendencia de Sociedades
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders must approve annual financial statements within three months after the year-end (by 31 March); the approved statements must be deposited with the commercial registry within one month after approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Untimely deposit or non-deposit is a registry infraction; the company and its legal representative may be fined, and third-party reliance on the filed financial statements is lost.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner information report (Información de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed annually in the same DIAN filing calendar as the income tax return; the exact due date depends on the NIT ending digit. Any change in ultimate beneficial ownership must be updated promptly.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omissions or incorrect information trigger DIAN penalties under the Colombian Tax Code and impair the company's ability to evidence valid withholding and transfer-pricing positions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For Colombian SAS, an independent statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory when, at 31 December of the preceding year, total gross assets exceed 5,000 SMLMV or total gross income exceeds 3,000 SMLMV; it is also mandatory if the company is subject to permanent inspection or surveillance by the Superintendencia de Sociedades. A SAS not crossing these thresholds is not legally required to appoint an auditor unless voluntarily agreed in the shareholders' agreement.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian version of IFRS: Decreto 2420 of 2015 and subsequent amendments. Cybersecurity SaaS companies below the public-accountability threshold normally apply NIIF para PYMES (Grupo 2); larger or supervised entities apply full IFRS (Grupo 1).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The legal representative must verify the shareholders' register before each annual meeting and confirm that transfers of shares have been recorded and the beneficiary ownership data reported. Annual confirmation is performed through the DIAN beneficial-owner declaration; a transfer not recorded in the registered share ledger and notified to the company is ineffective against the company and blocks the updated annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors and Board Minutes if a board exists (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Shareholders' Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea General)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – USD 6,500 per year (only if the audit threshold or Revisor Fiscal requirement is triggered; otherwise not incurred)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 35% general corporate income tax for Colombian Sociedades por Acciones Simplificadas with domestic tax residence.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No blanket statutory tax holiday is available. Preferential provisions include: 100% additional income-tax deduction for qualifying investments in research, technology and software development under Article 158-1 E.T.; 100% payroll deduction for new employees below age 28; availability of the 'Economía Naranja' income-tax exemption for qualifying new creative and software-related activities, subject to registration, revenue caps, and substance requirements; income-tax credit for VAT paid on productive fixed assets under Article 258-1 E.T.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios. Mandatory electronic filing through the DIAN online portal (SIRE) using an authorized digital certificate and electronic signature.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Fiscal year generally coincides with the calendar year ending on 31 December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Deadline falls within the ninth calendar month after the fiscal year-end. The exact date is fixed annually by DIAN based on the last two digits of the taxpayer's NIT, generally between 9 and 17 September of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number of the SAS, taxpayer name, and address of the principal Colombian establishment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident S.A.S. owner must use the same Colombian NIT of the entity. The foreign shareholder's identification and country of residence are filed in the supplementary shareholder information schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year ending date; normally 31 December.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Colombia-source income is included. Foreign income not deemed effectively connected to the Colombian SAS is excluded unless CFC rules apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross Colombian operational income from cybersecurity SaaS subscriptions, licensing, penetration testing, and related services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must not report the company's gross receipts on their own return; all Colombian service revenue is reported at the entity level. VAT-excluded export revenue is reported in the gross income annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, rebates, and discounts granted on billings, including chargebacks from Stripe and refunded subscriptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Documentary evidence must be kept with digital invoices and payment processor statements; non-resident support does not alter the Colombian entity's gross revenue recognition.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs, cloud infrastructure costs, salaries, third-party subcontracted security researchers, and administrative expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cost sharing or service fees paid to the foreign parent or affiliated cybersecurity lab are accepted only when back-to-back invoice, beneficial receipt, and arm's-length substance are demonstrated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory special deductions, including R&D software development deductions and Orange Economy exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Colombian entity must be the actual operator of the qualifying activity; a passive receivable of foreign royalties does not qualify for special deductions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income before tax depreciation and tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not taxed at this stage; the result is used to compute the Colombian entity's distributable profits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year loss carryforwards up to five fiscal years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A change of indirect foreign ownership may trigger a restriction on the use of Colombian tax losses under anti-trafficking rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after exemptions and carryforward compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For the non-resident shareholder, the share of Colombian taxable income is not separately assessed at the entity level; tax is deferred until dividend distribution.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line: Impuesto de Renta y Complementarios
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed using the 35% statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No tax credit for foreign income taxes is available at the Colombian entity level in respect of income derived solely from Colombian SaaS clients.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings suffered during the year and advance payments of CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The company must reconcile withholding certificates issued to foreign payees and recipients of Colombian-source payments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box: Saldo a Pagar o Saldo a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax payable or refundable position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refund of VAT on SaaS exports and income-tax overpayments may be requested when the DIAN profile shows a favorable balance; foreign shareholders must ensure corporate bank accounts and Stripe settlement accounts are registered with the Colombian entity's foreign-exchange rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of financial report accuracy and approval by a certified public accountant enrolled with the DIAN.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident manager or legal representative must sign the return jointly with the Colombian CPA; the CPA assumes joint liability for inexact or omitted information.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty under Article 641 E.T. equals 5% of the tax due per month or fraction of month of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due. When no tax is due, the penalty is 0.5% of gross assets or net equity, subject to a minimum of 20 UVT and maximum of 100 UVT. A return filed after formal DIAN summons incurs substantially higher penalties. In addition, statutory moratory interest accrues monthly on outstanding balances, and criminal sanctions apply for wilful omission or false returns.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% withholding on gross dividends paid from Colombian taxable profits to a non-resident individual or entity; an additional 5% withholding applies on distributions made out of profits that have not effectively borne corporate income tax. The combined withholding on excess distributions may reach 35% where the underlying profits were wholly untaxed at the entity level.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Colombia income tax treaty, the foreign beneficial owner must (i) obtain a valid Certificate of Tax Residence from the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction; (ii) present the certificate and a treaty-benefit claim form to the Colombian paying company before the payment date; (iii) confirm beneficial ownership, absence of a Colombian permanent establishment, and absence of back-to-back/conduit arrangements. The paying SAS must retain the evidence for at least five years. If treaty relief is not applied at source, the recipient may request a refund from DIAN within the ordinary statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Software and IP royalties paid to a foreign beneficiary are subject to statutory withholding of 20%; technical assistance and know-how services are generally subject to a 15% or 20% rate depending on the nature of the service. Interest paid to foreign financial institutions is withheld at 15%; interest paid to non-financial foreign lenders is withheld at 20%. Applicable DTA rates generally range between 10% and 15% for royalties and between 5% and 15% for interest, subject to domestic beneficial ownership formalities.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File preparation is triggered when the Colombian SAS meets any of: (i) gross income ≥ 100,000 UVT (approximately COP 4.71 billion for tax year 2024); (ii) gross assets ≥ 150,000 UVT; (iii) gross equity ≥ 150,000 UVT; or (iv) transactions with related parties located in tax havens or preferential regimes, regardless of thresholds. TP documentation and informational return are filed through Form 120. The UVT value for 2024 is COP 47,065.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not apply a Gulf-style Economic Substance Regulations framework. However, substance is mandatory under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule of Article 869 E.T., the beneficial-ownership requirement of tax treaties, permanent-establishment definitions, and the statutory conditions for R&D and Orange Economy exemptions. A cybersecurity SaaS enterprise must document real employees, physical or virtual office substance, strategic decision-making in Colombia, ownership of intellectual property, assumption of operational risk, and genuine pre-sales/post-sales activity. An empty corporate shell with back-to-back foreign contracts will be recharacterized or disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating Colombian-source subscription revenue, issuing or using false electronic invoices, fabricating cloud-infrastructure costs, booking fictitious payroll for ghost employees, or deliberately failing to file Form 110. Redirecting Colombian client payments to a related shell in a zero-tax jurisdiction without arm's-length compensation is also treated as tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may impose the inexactness penalty of up to 200% of the tax understated, joint liability for unpaid taxes, and forfeiture of tax benefits. Criminal prosecution for wilful tax fraud can result in imprisonment of up to 9 years, criminal fines, confiscation of proceeds, and disqualification from government contracts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives are jointly liable under Article 794 E.T. when they knowingly participate in the tax fraud. Courts may pierce the S.A.S. veil to seize personal assets; travel bans, asset freezes, and extradition procedures may be ordered once a criminal investigation begins.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Lack of Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Colombian S.A.S. with no employees, no physical premises, no Colombian management, with board decisions taken exclusively abroad, and with all contracts arranged to funnel income to offshore related parties. The entity purports to be a software developer but does not exercise real control over research, development, or delivery of cybersecurity services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the transaction or the entity under Article 869 E.T., reassess taxable income at 35%, deny VAT refunds on export services, impose literal penalties up to 200% of the difference, and refer the case for criminal investigation. The company may be declared a mere façade and liquidated.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who permit a zero-substance shell to accept foreign revenue become personally liable for the resulting tax debt and civil restitution. A formal finding of fiscal fraud may also trigger personal criminal responsibility, restrictions on leaving Colombia, and disqualification from holding corporate office.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Anti-Money Laundering and Foreign Exchange Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving wire transfers from Stripe or foreign clients into personal accounts of shareholders, failing to report to the Banco de la República on required inward foreign exchange declarations, ignoring UIAF cash-transaction threshold reporting, failing to identify the ultimate beneficial owner of the S.A.S., or processing transactions through unlicensed payment intermediaries to evade tax inspection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: UIAF and fiscal authorities may impose monetary fines per violation, block bank accounts, suspend the company's tax registration number, and order confiscation of funds. Money-laundering offences carry imprisonment from 6 to 15 years in Colombia, depending on aggravation, and the corporate entity may be dissolved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who control payment rails and ignore AML controls face personal criminal liability, civil restitution to victims, and asset forfeiture. Colombian courts may issue preventive travel bans, notification to Interpol, and broad seizure orders over foreign bank accounts.
